name: Kaguya (SELENE)
best_known_for: Japan's second lunar orbiter: mapped the Moon's surface, gravity and magnetism from polar orbit, and filmed Earth rising over the limb
credit: SELENE (Selenological and Engineering Explorer), nicknamed Kaguya after the lunar princess of The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter, was Japan's second lunar orbiter after Hiten. Launched on 2007-09-14 from Tanegashima on an H-IIA, the 2914 kg main orbiter carried two 53 kg subsatellites on its roof: Okina, a relay satellite, and Ouna, a radio source for VLBI tracking. After lunar orbit insertion on 2007-10-03 it settled into a circular polar orbit at 100 km on 2007-10-19. Its instrument suite included a terrain camera, a multiband imager, a spectral profiler, X-ray and gamma-ray spectrometers, a laser altimeter, a radar sounder and a magnetometer, and a high-definition television camera filmed the Earth rising over the lunar limb. Okina hit the far side on 2009-02-12; the main orbiter was commanded into a controlled impact near Gill crater on 2009-06-10.
